what: Equitable Holdings sells retirement and life products in the United States: variable annuities, employer retirement plans and life insurance. It also owns most of AllianceBernstein, the asset manager.
customers: Americans saving for retirement through financial advisers, employers running workplace plans, and institutions investing with AllianceBernstein.
money: retirement plans for schools and non-profits
moat: A distribution force of advisers and a book of policies that stay for decades, plus an asset manager that earns fees on the same money.
risks: Variable annuity profits depend on equity markets, so a bear market hits both fees and hedging
Reported earnings swing on hedge accounting rather than on the underlying business
$4.6B of debt, and an insurance balance sheet whose value moves with bond markets
opportunities: 10 times earnings and 5.3 times free cash flow, with $2.6B of free cash flow and $12.5B of cash
Analysts see about 26% upside, with 11 covering the stock
Registered index-linked annuities, where it is a leader, are the fastest-growing retirement product in America
watch: Annuity net flows and the AllianceBernstein fee base.
